question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the term with the variable exponent by dividing both sides by $2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot {6}^{k} & =72 \\ \frac{2\cdot {6}^{k}}{2} & =\frac{72}{2} \\ {6}^{k} & =36\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rewrite $36$ as ${6}^{2}$ to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{k} & =36 \\ {6}^{k} & ={6}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(6)$, we equate the exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{6}^{k} & ={6}^{2} \\ k & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $k=2.$
